![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/74c26773d49442671fcf6526764215523ca0231a7889671330a7ac539f3402fc.png)

A plate occupies the region $D$ enclosed by the $y$-axis and the lines $x=2y$ and $x=3-y$, as shown above. The mass density function of the plate is $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{y}{6}.$ Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $x=2.$
worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,\frac{x}{2}\le y\le 3-x},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/0c9efcbae53bdd2620b0bf7009ce4f4f2a20a38f393cac008899621ec391d261.png)

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-2|
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{x/2}^{3-x}(\frac{y}{6})|x-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{x/2}^{3-x}(\frac{y}{6})(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}-4x+4)[{\int }_{x/2}^{3-x}\frac{y}{6}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}-4x+4){[\frac{{y}^{2}}{12}]}_{x/2}^{3-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}-4x+4)[\frac{(3-x)^{2}}{12}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{48}]\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{48}{\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}-4x+4)(36-24x+3{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{48}{\int }_{0}^{2}3{x}^{4}-36{x}^{3}+144{x}^{2}-240x+144\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{5}}{80}-\frac{3{x}^{4}}{16}+{x}^{3}-\frac{5{x}^{2}}{2}+3x]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =(\frac{2}{5}-3+8-10+6)-0 \\  & =\frac{7}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
